subject: Cloud Computing
title: Data Loss Prevention
description: Learn Data Loss Prevention in one minute.

hook.text: An employee emails a spreadsheet with 10,000 customer credit card numbers. DLP could have stopped it.

buildup.text: Data Loss Prevention tools scan data in motion, at rest, and in use to detect sensitive information.

discovery.text: DLP can identify credit card numbers, social security numbers, and health data — then block or alert.

twist.text: DLP generates mountains of false positives. Tuning it to be useful without being annoying is an art.

climax.text: In the cloud, DLP extends to storage buckets, databases, and SaaS apps. The surface area is enormous.

punchline.text: DLP watches for data leaving where it shouldn't. It's a safety net.

quiz.question: What is the main challenge of implementing DLP?
options: Tuning it to minimize false positives while still catching real threats
DLP tools can only scan email, not cloud storage
DLP makes all data access completely impossible

details.summary: DLP tools detect and prevent sensitive data from leaving cloud environments through unauthorized channels. They scan storage, email, and network traffic for patterns like credit card numbers, personal identifiers, and confidential documents to block exfiltration.
details.whyItMatters: Data exfiltration is the ultimate goal of most attacks. DLP provides the last line of defense to prevent sensitive data from leaving the organization even if other controls fail.
takeaways: DLP scans for sensitive data patterns across cloud services
It blocks unauthorized sharing, copying, or downloading
Classification labels help DLP identify what to protect

faq.question: How does cloud DLP identify sensitive data?
faq.answer: DLP uses pattern matching for known formats like credit card numbers, machine learning classifiers for unstructured data, and data classification labels assigned by users or automated tools. It can scan cloud storage, SaaS applications, and network traffic simultaneously.

faq.question: Does DLP require classifying all data first?
faq.answer: Classification improves accuracy but is not strictly required. DLP can detect many sensitive data types automatically through pattern recognition. However, implementing a classification scheme that labels data by sensitivity level significantly reduces false positives.
